content:
The image shows a cross-sectional/longitudinal view of soybean stems split open, with a ruler at the top for scale. Key features:

- **Stems split lengthwise**, showing internal tissue
- **Top stem**: white/cream pith — healthy-looking internally
- **Bottom two stems**: reddish-brown to dark brown discoloration of the internal pith and vascular tissue
- The discoloration runs continuously through the pith
- External stem appearance seems relatively normal (hairy stem surface visible)

This internal browning of pith visible when stems are split is the classic diagnostic feature. Now comparing:

- **Brown Stem Rot**: Internal browning of pith and vascular tissue when stems are split; healthy white pith = healthy, brown pith = BSR. The description states "Healthy stems have white pith, while BSR-infected stems have brown pith."
- **Sudden Death Syndrome**: White pith when cut — explicitly distinguishes from BSR by having **white** pith.

The image shows the contrast: one stem with white pith (healthy or used as control) and two stems with reddish-brown pith — exactly matching the Brown Stem Rot diagnostic comparison image.

This internal browning pattern is the hallmark diagnostic feature of Brown Stem Rot. SDS is ruled out because it produces white pith when cut."}
